paragraphs.text: בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לְאָחָ֖ז מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ הוֹשֵׁ֨עַ בֶּן־אֵלָ֧ה בְשֹׁמְר֛וֹן עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תֵּ֥שַׁע שָׁנִֽים׃

i18n.en: In the twelfth year of Achaz king of Yehudah, Hoshea son of Elah began to reign in Shomron over Yisra'el, for nine years.

notes.official:
Names in this chapter: Achaz = Ahaz; Yehudah = Judah; Hoshea = Hoshea; Elah = Elah; Shomron = Samaria; Yisra'el = Israel; Shalman'eser = Shalmaneser; Ashur = Assyria; So = So; Mitzrayim = Egypt; Par'oh = Pharaoh; Chalach = Halah; Chavor = Habor; Gozan = Gozan; Madai = the Medes; Yarov'am = Jeroboam; Nevat = Nebat; Bavel = Babylon; Kutah / Kut = Cuthah / Cuth; Avva = Avva; Chamat = Hamath; Sefarvayim = Sepharvaim; Beit-El = Bethel; Ya'aqov = Jacob (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`). The draft's 'Shomeron' is normalized to Shomron, the form used in 1 Kgs 16-22 and 2 Kgs 1-2.

*bišnaṯ šətêm ʿeśrēh ləʾāḥāz* 'In the twelfth year of Achaz'. The synchronism conflicts with 15:30 (Hoshea's accession in the twentieth year of Yotam) and with 18:1, 9-10; the chronology of the last kings of Israel is notoriously difficult (Thiele, *The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings*, 1983; Cogan and Tadmor, *II Kings*, AB 11, 1988). The MT figures are translated without harmonization.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה רַ֗ק לֹ֚א כְּמַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ לְפָנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And he did what was evil in the eyes of YHWH, yet not like the kings of Yisra'el who were before him.

notes.official: *raq lōʾ kəmalḵê yiśrāʾēl* 'yet not like the kings of Yisra'el who were before him': the only qualified condemnation of a northern king; the text gives no reason.

paragraphs.text: עָלָ֣יו עָלָ֔ה שַׁלְמַנְאֶ֖סֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַֽיְהִי־ל֤וֹ הוֹשֵׁ֙עַ֙ עֶ֔בֶד וַיָּ֥שֶׁב ל֖וֹ מִנְחָֽה׃

i18n.en: Against him came up Shalman'eser king of Ashur; and Hoshea became his servant and paid him tribute.

notes.official: *šalmanʾeser meleḵ ʾaššûr* 'Shalman'eser king of Ashur': Shalmaneser V (727-722 BCE). *wayyāšeḇ lô minḥâ* 'and paid him tribute': *minḥâ* in the political sense of tribute (cf. 1 Kgs 5:1); the Genesis-scoped minḥâ entries do not govern it.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּמְצָא֩ מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֨וּר בְּהוֹשֵׁ֜עַ קֶ֗שֶׁר אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֤ח מַלְאָכִים֙ אֶל־ס֣וֹא מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֔יִם וְלֹא־הֶעֱלָ֥ה מִנְחָ֛ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר כְּשָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֑ה וַֽיַּעַצְרֵ֙הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיַּאַסְרֵ֖הוּ בֵּ֥ית כֶּֽלֶא׃

i18n.en: And the king of Ashur found conspiracy in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So king of Mitzrayim, and had not brought up tribute to the king of Ashur as he had year by year; so the king of Ashur shut him up and bound him in prison.

notes.official: *ʾel-sôʾ meleḵ-miṣrayim* 'to So king of Mitzrayim'. No Egyptian king named So is known. Proposals include Osorkon IV of Tanis (Kitchen, *The Third Intermediate Period in Egypt*, 1973), an abbreviation of a royal name, or the city of Sais, read as 'to Sais, (to) the king of Egypt' (Goedicke, *BASOR* 171, 1963; Cogan and Tadmor); the personal-name reading of the MT and the ASV is kept. *qešer* 'conspiracy'. *bêṯ keleʾ* 'prison'. *malʾāḵîm* 'messengers', human envoys (central `malakh-yhwh-messenger`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥עַל מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֖וּר בְּכָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיַּ֙עַל֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וַיָּ֥צַר עָלֶ֖יהָ שָׁלֹ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃

i18n.en: Then the king of Ashur came up against all the land, and went up to Shomron and besieged it three years.

notes.official: *wayyaʿal meleḵ-ʾaššûr bəḵol-hāʾāreṣ* 'Then the king of Ashur came up against all the land' (central `eretz`). *wayyāṣar ʿālêhā šālōš šānîm* 'and besieged it three years', c. 724-722 BCE.

paragraphs.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת הַתְּשִׁיעִ֜ית לְהוֹשֵׁ֗עַ לָכַ֤ד מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁוּר֙ אֶת־שֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַיֶּ֥גֶל אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַשּׁ֑וּרָה וַיֹּ֨שֶׁב אֹתָ֜ם בַּחְלַ֧ח וּבְחָב֛וֹר נְהַ֥ר גּוֹזָ֖ן וְעָרֵ֥י מָדָֽי׃ (פ)

i18n.en: In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Ashur took Shomron, and carried Yisra'el away into exile to Ashur, and settled them in Chalach, and on the Chavor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of Madai.

notes.official:
*lāḵaḏ meleḵ-ʾaššûr ʾeṯ-šōmərôn* 'the king of Ashur took Shomron'. The Babylonian Chronicle credits Shalmaneser V with the destruction of Samaria, while Sargon II (722-705) claims its capture and the deportation of 27,290 people in his annals; the 'king of Ashur' here may be either, and the event is dated 722/720 BCE (Tadmor, *JCS* 12, 1958; Becking, *The Fall of Samaria*, 1992). *wayyeḡel ʾeṯ-yiśrāʾēl ʾaššûrâ* 'and carried Yisra'el away into exile to Ashur'.

*baḥlaḥ ûḇəḥāḇôr nəhar gôzān wəʿārê māḏāy* 'in Chalach, and on the Chavor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of Madai': Halah near Nineveh, the Habur river with the city of Gozan (Tell Halaf), and the towns of the Medes in western Iran. *māḏāy* is the Hebrew name of the Medes (Gen 10:2), transliterated here (ASV 'the Medes'). The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) closes the report; vv 7-23 are the Deuteronomistic reflection on the fall of the northern kingdom.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּֽי־חָטְא֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֔ם הַמַּעֲלֶ֤ה אֹתָם֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מִתַּ֕חַת יַ֖ד פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּֽירְא֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִֽים׃

i18n.en: And this came about because the children of Yisra'el had sinned against YHWH their Elohim, who brought them up out of the land of Mitzrayim from under the hand of Par'oh king of Mitzrayim, and they had feared other elohim,

notes.official: *wayyîrəʾû ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm* 'and they had feared other elohim'. Gods other than YHWH are written in lower case in the Kings convention (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 4), following exodus-woh at Ex 20:3 (central `elohim-aherim-other-gods-monolatry-vs-monotheism-scholarly-dispute-cross-corpus`; also vv 35, 37, 38). *mittaḥaṯ yaḏ parʿōh* 'from under the hand of Par'oh': Kings transliterates the title (exodus-woh's 'Pharaoh' is a single-book exception, as with 'Moses'; `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ בְּחֻקּ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשֽׂוּ׃

i18n.en: and walked in the statutes of the nations whom YHWH dispossessed from before the children of Yisra'el, and of the kings of Yisra'el, which they made.

notes.official: *ûmalḵê yiśrāʾēl ʾăšer ʿāśû* 'and of the kings of Yisra'el, which they made': the syntax is compressed and the clause may be a gloss (Burney; Cogan and Tadmor); the ASV construal is kept.

paragraphs.text: וַיְחַפְּא֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל דְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־כֵ֔ן עַל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּבְנ֨וּ לָהֶ֤ם בָּמוֹת֙ בְּכָל־עָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם מִמִּגְדַּ֥ל נוֹצְרִ֖ים עַד־עִ֥יר מִבְצָֽר׃

i18n.en: And the children of Yisra'el did secretly things that were not right against YHWH their Elohim; and they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city;

notes.official: *wayḥappəʾû ... dəḇārîm ʾăšer lōʾ-ḵēn* 'And the children of Yisra'el did secretly things that were not right'. *ḥpʾ* occurs only here; the ASV 'did secretly' relates it to *ḥpy* / *ḥph* 'cover', and other proposals are 'attributed (falsely)' or 'uttered' (HALOT; Cogan and Tadmor). The ASV sense is kept. *bāmôṯ* 'high places' (ASV), local cult sites, as in 1 Kgs 13 and 22 (also vv 11, 29, 32). *mimmiḡdal nôṣərîm ʿaḏ-ʿîr miḇṣār* 'from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city', i.e. everywhere, from the smallest outpost to the walled town.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּצִּ֧בוּ לָהֶ֛ם מַצֵּב֖וֹת וַאֲשֵׁרִ֑ים עַ֚ל כָּל־גִּבְעָ֣ה גְבֹהָ֔ה וְתַ֖חַת כָּל־עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָֽן׃

i18n.en: and they set up for themselves pillars and Asherim on every high hill and under every leafy tree;

notes.official: *maṣṣēḇôṯ* 'pillars' (central `matzevah-sacred-pillar-patriarchal-religion`, whose rationale traces the patriarchal standing-stone to its Deuteronomic prohibition, Deut 16:22). *wăʾăšērîm* 'and Asherim': wooden cult objects associated with the goddess Asherah (Deut 16:21), here plural (cf. v 16 'an Asherah'); Asherah is kept in its English form in Kings (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`; central `athirat-asherah-mother-goddess-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible` for the Ugaritic goddess). *ʿal kol-giḇʿâ ḡəḇōhâ wəṯaḥaṯ kol-ʿēṣ raʿănān* 'on every high hill and under every leafy tree', the Deuteronomic formula (Deut 12:2; 1 Kgs 14:23).

paragraphs.text: וַיְקַטְּרוּ־שָׁם֙ בְּכָל־בָּמ֔וֹת כַּגּוֹיִ֕ם אֲשֶׁר־הֶגְלָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֙ דְּבָרִ֣ים רָעִ֔ים לְהַכְעִ֖יס אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: and there they burned incense on all the high places, like the nations whom YHWH carried away before them; and they did evil things to provoke YHWH to anger;

notes.official: *wayqaṭṭərû* 'they burned incense' (or 'made offerings smoke'). *kaggôyim ʾăšer-heḡlâ YHWH mip̄nêhem* 'like the nations whom YHWH carried away before them': the verb *glh* Hiphil 'exile' is the keyword of the chapter (vv 6, 11, 23, 26, 27, 28, 33).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּֽעַבְד֖וּ הַגִּלֻּלִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לָהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: and they served the idols, of which YHWH had said to them, "You shall not do this thing."

notes.official: *haggillulîm* 'the idols': a derogatory word, often explained from *gll* 'dung' or 'roll' ('dung-things' / 'blocks'), frequent in Ezekiel (Ezek 6:4-13). The ASV 'idols' is kept.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣עַד יְהוָ֡ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל וּבִיהוּדָ֡ה בְּיַד֩ כָּל־נביאו [נְבִיאֵ֨י] כָל־חֹזֶ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר שֻׁ֝֠בוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֤ם הָֽרָעִים֙ וְשִׁמְרוּ֙ מִצְוֺתַ֣י חֻקּוֹתַ֔י כְּכָ֨ל־הַתּוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי אֶת־אֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם וַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁלַ֣חְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד עֲבָדַ֥י הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃

i18n.en: Yet YHWH testified to Yisra'el and to Yehudah by the hand of every prophet and every seer, saying, "Turn from your evil ways, and keep my commandments, my statutes, according to all the law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by the hand of my servants the prophets."

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *nbyʾw* 'his prophets' / Qere *nəḇîʾê* 'prophets of'; the Qere is translated in the ASV construal, 'by the hand of every prophet and every seer' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

*wayyāʿaḏ YHWH* 'Yet YHWH testified': *ʿwd* Hiphil 'warn solemnly, call to witness'. *ḥōzeh* 'seer'. *kəḵol-hattôrâ* 'according to all the law': in the Deuteronomistic History *tôrâ* is the written law of Moshe (1 Kgs 2:3; 2 Kgs 17:37 'which he wrote for you'), and Kings keeps the ASV 'law' (`torah-law-deuteronomistic-kings`); exodus-woh transliterates 'torah' at Ex 13:9; 16:4, a divergence recorded in that entry. *ʿăḇāḏay hannəḇîʾîm* 'my servants the prophets' (central `navi-first-occurrence-abraham`).

paragraphs.text: וְלֹ֖א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ וַיַּקְשׁ֤וּ אֶת־עָרְפָּם֙ כְּעֹ֣רֶף אֲבוֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א הֶאֱמִ֔ינוּ בַּֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: But they did not listen, and stiffened their neck like the neck of their fathers, who did not trust in YHWH their Elohim.

notes.official: *wayyaqšû ʾeṯ-ʿorpām kəʿōrep̄ ʾăḇôṯām* 'and stiffened their neck like the neck of their fathers' (Ex 32:9; Deut 10:16). *ʾăšer lōʾ heʾĕmînû bayhwh* 'who did not trust in YHWH' (cf. Num 14:11; Deut 1:32).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּמְאֲס֣וּ אֶת־חֻקָּ֗יו וְאֶת־בְּרִיתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרַ֣ת אֶת־אֲבוֹתָ֔ם וְאֵת֙ עֵֽדְוֺתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵעִ֖יד בָּ֑ם וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ אַחֲרֵ֤י הַהֶ֙בֶל֙ וַיֶּהְבָּ֔לוּ וְאַחֲרֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר סְבִֽיבֹתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֹתָ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֖י עֲשׂ֥וֹת כָּהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And they rejected his statutes, and his covenant which he cut with their fathers, and his testimonies which he testified against them; and they went after vanity and became vain, and after the nations that were around them, concerning whom YHWH had commanded them not to do like them.

notes.official: *wəʾeṯ-bərîṯô ʾăšer kāraṯ ʾeṯ-ʾăḇôṯām* 'and his covenant which he cut with their fathers' (central `karat-brit-cut-covenant`). *ʿēḏəwōṯāyw ʾăšer hēʿîḏ bām* 'his testimonies which he testified against them', the same root as v 13. *wayyēlḵû ʾaḥărê hahebel wayyehbālû* 'and they went after vanity and became vain' (ASV): *hebel* is 'breath, vapour, futility', and the verb is formed from the noun, so they became what they followed; the same wordplay occurs at Jer 2:5. The ASV pair keeps the paronomasia.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעַזְב֗וּ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם מַסֵּכָ֖ה שנים [שְׁנֵ֣י] עֲגָלִ֑ים וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ אֲשֵׁירָ֗ה וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲווּ֙ לְכָל־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיַּעַבְד֖וּ אֶת־הַבָּֽעַל׃

i18n.en: And they forsook all the commandments of YHWH their Elohim, and made for themselves molten images, two calves; and they made an Asherah, and worshipped all the host of the heavens, and served Ba'al.

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *šnym* 'two' (absolute) / Qere *šənê* 'two (of)' (construct) (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

*wayyaʿăśû lāhem massēḵâ šənê ʿăḡālîm* 'and made for themselves molten images, two calves': *massēḵâ* 'cast image' is singular, used collectively in apposition to 'two calves' (the calves of Beit-El and Dan, 1 Kgs 12:28-29; cf. Ex 32:4 *ʿēḡel massēḵâ*); the ASV plural is kept. *wayyaʿăśû ʾăšêrâ* 'and they made an Asherah' (v 10).

*wayyištaḥăwû ləḵol-ṣəḇāʾ haššāmayim* 'and worshipped all the host of the heavens' (draft 'skies'). Here the phrase names the stars and celestial bodies as objects of worship (Deut 4:19; 17:3; 2 Kgs 21:3, 5; 23:4-5); the same phrase names YHWH's council at 1 Kgs 22:19, and in ANE thought the two senses were related (Job 38:7). One rendering is used for both, so that the reader sees the same Hebrew phrase in both places (central `tzeva-ha-shamayim-host-of-the-heavens-divine-council-cross-corpus`, extended in this pass; `shamayim`, numinous register). *wayyaʿaḇḏû ʾeṯ-habbāʿal* 'and served Ba'al' (draft 'Baal'): the Kings spelling, without the English article (`habbaal-baal-hebrew-bible-rendering-kings`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** Before quoting v 23, The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) summarises Israel's apostasy by saying the people 'worshipped metal idols' (French 'des idoles en métal'). The nearest Hebrew in this chapter is *massēḵâ* 'molten (cast) image' here; the line keeps the ASV rendering and does not encode the reading.

paragraphs.text: וַֽ֠יַּעֲבִירוּ אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֤ם וְאֶת־בְּנֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וַיִּקְסְמ֥וּ קְסָמִ֖ים וַיְנַחֵ֑שׁוּ וַיִּֽתְמַכְּר֗וּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִיסֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And they made their sons and their daughters pass through the fire, and practised divination and divined, and sold themselves to do what was evil in the eyes of YHWH, to provoke him to anger.

notes.official: *wayyaʿăḇîrû ʾeṯ-bənêhem wəʾeṯ-bənôṯêhem bāʾēš* 'And they made their sons and their daughters pass through the fire', the child-sacrifice condemned in Deut 18:10 (cf. v 31; 16:3; 21:6). *wayyiqsəmû qəsāmîm wayənaḥēšû* 'and practised divination and divined': *qesem* is divination in general (with a cognate accusative), and *nḥš* Piel is the technical term for seeking omens (central `nichesh-laban-divination`, whose rationale cites this verse; ASV 'used divination and enchantments'). Both practices are listed together in Deut 18:10. *wayyiṯmakkərû* 'and sold themselves'.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתְאַנַּ֨ף יְהוָ֤ה מְאֹד֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיְסִרֵ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו לֹ֣א נִשְׁאַ֔ר רַ֛ק שֵׁ֥בֶט יְהוּדָ֖ה לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: So YHWH was very angry with Yisra'el, and removed them from his sight; none was left but the tribe of Yehudah alone.

notes.official: *wayyiṯʾannap̄ YHWH məʾōḏ* 'So YHWH was very angry'. *wayəsīrēm mēʿal pānāyw* 'and removed them from his sight' (also vv 20, 23). *lōʾ nišʾar raq šēḇeṭ yəhûḏâ ləḇaddô* 'none was left but the tribe of Yehudah alone' (cf. 1 Kgs 11:13, 32).

paragraphs.text: גַּם־יְהוּדָ֕ה לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔ר אֶת־מִצְוֺ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ בְּחֻקּ֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשֽׂוּ׃

i18n.en: Yehudah too did not keep the commandments of YHWH their Elohim, but walked in the statutes of Yisra'el which they made.

notes.official: Verses 19-20 extend the indictment to Yehudah and are widely seen as an exilic addition anticipating 587 BCE (Cogan and Tadmor).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּמְאַ֨ס יְהוָ֜ה בְּכָל־זֶ֤רַע יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיְעַנֵּ֔ם וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיַד־שֹׁסִ֑ים עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁלִיכָ֖ם מִפָּנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And YHWH rejected all the seed of Yisra'el, and afflicted them, and gave them into the hand of plunderers, until he had cast them out of his sight.

notes.official: *bəyaḏ-šōsîm* 'into the hand of plunderers'.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־קָרַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵעַל֙ בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֔ד וַיַּמְלִ֖יכוּ אֶת־יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֑ט וידא [וַיַּדַּ֨ח] יָרָבְעָ֤ם אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְהֶחֱטֵיאָ֖ם חֲטָאָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃

i18n.en: For he tore Yisra'el from the house of David; and they made Yarov'am son of Nevat king; and Yarov'am drove Yisra'el away from following YHWH, and made them sin a great sin.

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *wydʾ* (from *ndh* / *ndʾ*, 'and he thrust away') / Qere *wayyaddaḥ* 'and he drove away'; the Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

*kî-qāraʿ yiśrāʾēl mēʿal bêṯ dāwiḏ* 'For he tore Yisra'el from the house of David' (ASV 'he rent'). The subject is unexpressed: the ASV and most commentators supply YHWH, who 'tears' the kingdom in the Achiyah oracle (1 Kgs 11:11-13, 30-31); others take Yisra'el as the subject, 'Israel broke away'. 'Tore' keeps the *qrʿ* keyword of the Yarov'am narrative, as at 1 Kgs 13:3, 5 (1-kings-woh overlay `niqra-ha-mizbeach-the-altar-torn-1-kings-13`). *wehĕḥĕṭîʾām ḥăṭāʾâ ḡəḏōlâ* 'and made them sin a great sin' (1 Kgs 14:16).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּכָל־חַטֹּ֥אות יָרָבְעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה לֹא־סָ֖רוּ מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

i18n.en: And the children of Yisra'el walked in all the sins of Yarov'am which he did; they did not turn aside from them,

notes.official: *bəḵol-ḥaṭṭōʾwṯ yārāḇʿām* 'in all the sins of Yarov'am', the refrain of the northern regnal summaries (1 Kgs 15:30; 16:31).

paragraphs.text: עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁר־הֵסִ֨יר יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֔יו כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד כָּל־עֲבָדָ֣יו הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים וַיִּ֨גֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל מֵעַ֤ל אַדְמָתוֹ֙ אַשּׁ֔וּרָה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: until YHWH removed Yisra'el from his sight, as he had spoken by the hand of all his servants the prophets. So Yisra'el was carried away into exile from its own land to Ashur, unto this day.

notes.official:
*kaʾăšer dibber bəyaḏ kol-ʿăḇāḏāyw hannəḇîʾîm* 'as he had spoken by the hand of all his servants the prophets' (central `navi-first-occurrence-abraham`). *wayyiḡel yiśrāʾēl mēʿal ʾaḏmāṯô ʾaššûrâ ʿaḏ hayyôm hazzeh* 'So Yisra'el was carried away into exile from its own land to Ashur, unto this day' (`ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh-aetiological-formula`). *ʾăḏāmâ* is the people's own soil. The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) closes the reflection.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('and Israel was carried away out of their own land') as the consequence of Israel's turning away from its creators. The translation renders the Hebrew as the ASV does and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֵ֣א מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֡וּר מִבָּבֶ֡ל וּ֠מִכּוּ֠תָה וּמֵעַוָּ֤א וּמֵֽחֲמָת֙ וּסְפַרְוַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֙שֶׁב֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן תַּ֖חַת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּֽרְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־שֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַיֵּֽשְׁב֖וּ בְּעָרֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And the king of Ashur brought people from Bavel, and from Kutah, and from Avva, and from Chamat, and Sefarvayim, and settled them in the cities of Shomron in place of the children of Yisra'el; and they took possession of Shomron and dwelt in its cities.

notes.official: *mibbāḇel ûmikkûṯâ ûmēʿawwāʾ ûmēḥămāṯ ûsəp̄arwāyim* 'from Bavel, and from Kutah, and from Avva, and from Chamat, and Sefarvayim'. Babylon and Cuthah (Tell Ibrahim, cult centre of Nergal, v 30) are in Babylonia; Hamath is in Syria; Avva and Sefarvayim are uncertain, perhaps Syrian towns (Sefarvayim possibly Sibraim, Ezek 47:16) rather than Babylonian Sippar (Cogan and Tadmor). Sargon II's annals report the resettlement of conquered peoples in Samaria. The town is *kûṯâ* here and *kûṯ* at v 30; both MT forms are kept.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּתְחִלַּת֙ שִׁבְתָּ֣ם שָׁ֔ם לֹ֥א יָרְא֖וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיְשַׁלַּ֨ח יְהוָ֤ה בָּהֶם֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֲרָי֔וֹת וַיִּֽהְי֥וּ הֹרְגִ֖ים בָּהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they did not fear YHWH; so YHWH sent lions among them, and they were killing some of them.

notes.official: *wayšallaḥ YHWH bāhem ʾeṯ-hāʾărāyôṯ* 'so YHWH sent lions among them': lions as the agents of divine judgement, as at 1 Kgs 13:24 and 20:36. The narrator names YHWH as the sender.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֮ לֵאמֹר֒ הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִגְלִ֙יתָ֙ וַתּ֙וֹשֶׁב֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֔וֹן לֹ֣א יָֽדְע֔וּ אֶת־מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיְשַׁלַּח־בָּ֣ם אֶת־הָאֲרָי֗וֹת וְהִנָּם֙ מְמִיתִ֣ים אוֹתָ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ אֵינָ֣ם יֹדְעִ֔ים אֶת־מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: So they spoke to the king of Ashur, saying, "The nations whom you have carried away and settled in the cities of Shomron do not know the manner of the Elohim of the land; therefore he has sent lions among them, and behold, they are killing them, because they do not know the manner of the Elohim of the land."

notes.official:
*lōʾ yāḏəʿû ʾeṯ-mišpaṭ ʾĕlōhê hāʾāreṣ* 'do not know the manner of the Elohim of the land' (draft 'the law'; ASV 'the law of the god of the land'; KJV 'the manner of the God of the land'). *mišpāṭ* here is the customary rite or practice owed to a territorial deity, the same noun as 'manner' in vv 33, 34, 40 ('according to the manner of the nations', 'the former manners'); 'manner' keeps that thread, which is the irony of the episode, and leaves 'law' for *tôrâ* (vv 13, 34, 37) (`mishpat-manner-custom-2-kings-17`).

*ʾĕlōhê hāʾāreṣ* 'the Elohim of the land': the speakers think of a local god, but the narrator has just said that YHWH sent the lions (v 25), so the Kings convention for a YHWH referent with a possessor applies ('the Elohim of Yisra'el'; `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 3). The singular verb *wayšallaḥ* 'he has sent' agrees. The ASV lower-case 'god' expresses the settlers' perspective, which the commentary records.

paragraphs.text: וַיְצַ֨ו מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֜וּר לֵאמֹ֗ר הֹלִ֤יכוּ שָׁ֙מָּה֙ אֶחָ֤ד מֵהַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִגְלִיתֶ֣ם מִשָּׁ֔ם וְיֵלְכ֖וּ וְיֵ֣שְׁבוּ שָׁ֑ם וְיֹרֵ֕ם אֶת־מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: Then the king of Ashur commanded, saying, "Carry there one of the priests whom you carried away from there; and let them go and dwell there, and let him teach them the manner of the Elohim of the land."

notes.official: *hōlîḵû šāmmâ ʾeḥāḏ mēhakkōhănîm* 'Carry there one of the priests': the plural verbs *wəyēlḵû wəyēšəḇû* 'and let them go and dwell there' are followed by singular *wəyōrēm* 'and let him teach them'; the versions harmonize, and the MT is translated. *ʾeṯ-mišpaṭ ʾĕlōhê hāʾāreṣ* 'the manner of the Elohim of the land' (`mishpat-manner-custom-2-kings-17`; see v 26).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֞א אֶחָ֣ד מֵהַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִגְלוּ֙ מִשֹּׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֑ל וַֽיְהִי֙ מוֹרֶ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם אֵ֖יךְ יִֽירְא֥וּ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: So one of the priests whom they had carried away from Shomron came and dwelt in Beit-El, and taught them how they should fear YHWH.

notes.official: *wayyēšeḇ bəḇêṯ-ʾēl* 'and dwelt in Beit-El', the royal sanctuary of the calf cult (1 Kgs 12:29; central `bethel-luz-name-etymology`). *wayəhî môreh ʾōṯām* 'and taught them' (*yrh*, the root of *tôrâ*).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּהְי֣וּ עֹשִׂ֔ים גּ֥וֹי גּ֖וֹי אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיַּנִּ֣יחוּ ׀ בְּבֵ֣ית הַבָּמ֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ הַשֹּׁ֣מְרֹנִ֔ים גּ֥וֹי גּוֹי֙ בְּעָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥ם יֹשְׁבִ֖ים שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: But every nation made elohim of its own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Shomronites had made, every nation in their cities in which they dwelt.

notes.official: *wayyihyû ʿōśîm gôy gôy ʾĕlōhāyw* 'But every nation made elohim of its own' (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 4). *haššōmərōnîm* 'the Shomronites' (draft 'Shomronim'; ASV 'the Samaritans'): the gentilic of Shomron, here the former Israelite inhabitants who had built the high places, not the later Samaritan community; the word occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible. Gentilics take English '-ite' in Kings, and the transliterated stem avoids the anachronism of 'Samaritans' (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בָבֶ֗ל עָשׂוּ֙ אֶת־סֻכּ֣וֹת בְּנ֔וֹת וְאַנְשֵׁי־כ֔וּת עָשׂ֖וּ אֶת־נֵֽרְגַ֑ל וְאַנְשֵׁ֥י חֲמָ֖ת עָשׂ֥וּ אֶת־אֲשִׁימָֽא׃

i18n.en: And the men of Bavel made Sukkot-Benot, and the men of Kut made Nergal, and the men of Chamat made Ashima,

notes.official: The settlers' deities, transliterated in their Hebrew forms (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`): *sukkôṯ bənôṯ* Sukkot-Benot (ASV Succoth-benoth), unexplained, often taken as a deformation of the name of a Babylonian goddess such as Zarpanitu, or as 'booths of daughters'; *nērḡal* Nergal, the underworld god of Cuthah; *ʾăšîmāʾ* Ashima of Hamath (cf. Amos 8:14 'the guilt [*ʾašmaṯ*] of Shomron') (Cogan and Tadmor). The verb *ʿāśû* 'made' (vv 29-32) is used both of making idols and, at v 32, of officiating.

paragraphs.text: וְהָעַוִּ֛ים עָשׂ֥וּ נִבְחַ֖ז וְאֶת־תַּרְתָּ֑ק וְהַסְפַרְוִ֗ים שֹׂרְפִ֤ים אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶם֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ לְאַדְרַמֶּ֥לֶךְ וַֽעֲנַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אלה [אֱלֹהֵ֥י] ספרים [סְפַרְוָֽיִם׃]

i18n.en: and the Avvites made Nivchaz and Tartaq; and the Sefarvites burned their children in the fire to Adrammelekh and Anammelekh, the elohim of Sefarvayim.

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *ʾlh sprym* / Qere *ʾĕlōhê səp̄arwāyim* 'the elohim of Sefarvayim'; the Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). The sof pasuq inside the bracketed Qere in the text field is kept as delivered (see 4:5).

*wəhāʿawwîm* 'and the Avvites' and *wəhasəp̄arwîm* 'and the Sefarvites' (draft 'the Avvim', 'the Sefarvim'; ASV 'the Avvites', 'the Sepharvites'): gentilic '-ite' (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`). *niḇḥaz* Nivchaz and *tartāq* Tartaq are otherwise unknown. *śōrəp̄îm ʾeṯ-bənêhem bāʾēš* 'burned their children in the fire' (cf. v 17). *ʾaḏrammeleḵ waʿănammeleḵ* Adrammelekh and Anammelekh (ASV Adrammelech, Anammelech): the second element is *meleḵ* 'king' (or the deity Malik); Adrammelekh may reflect Adad-milki, Anammelekh Anu-malik (Cogan and Tadmor). *ʾĕlōhê səp̄arwāyim* 'the elohim of Sefarvayim', lower case (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 4).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּהְי֥וּ יְרֵאִ֖ים אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ לָהֶ֤ם מִקְצוֹתָם֙ כֹּהֲנֵ֣י בָמ֔וֹת וַיִּהְי֛וּ עֹשִׂ֥ים לָהֶ֖ם בְּבֵ֥ית הַבָּמֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And they feared YHWH, and made for themselves from among all of them priests of the high places, who sacrificed for them in the houses of the high places.

notes.official: *wayyaʿăśû lāhem miqṣôṯām kōhănê ḇāmôṯ* 'and made for themselves from among all of them priests of the high places' (cf. 1 Kgs 12:31). *wayyihyû ʿōśîm lāhem* 'who sacrificed for them' (ASV): *ʿāśâ* 'do, make' in the cultic sense 'offer, officiate' (BDB *ʿāśâ* I 1i; Ex 29:36; 1 Kgs 8:64).

paragraphs.text: אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה הָי֣וּ יְרֵאִ֑ים וְאֶת־אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶם֙ הָי֣וּ עֹֽבְדִ֔ים כְּמִשְׁפַּט֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הִגְל֥וּ אֹתָ֖ם מִשָּֽׁם׃

i18n.en: They feared YHWH, and served their own elohim, according to the manner of the nations from among whom they had been carried away.

notes.official: *ʾeṯ-YHWH hāyû yərēʾîm wəʾeṯ-ʾĕlōhêhem hāyû ʿōḇəḏîm* 'They feared YHWH, and served their own elohim' (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 4). *kəmišpaṭ haggôyim* 'according to the manner of the nations' (`mishpat-manner-custom-2-kings-17`).

paragraphs.text: עַ֣ד הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ הֵ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים כַּמִּשְׁפָּטִ֖ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֑ים אֵינָ֤ם יְרֵאִים֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה וְאֵינָ֣ם עֹשִׂ֗ים כְּחֻקֹּתָם֙ וּכְמִשְׁפָּטָ֔ם וְכַתּוֹרָ֣ה וְכַמִּצְוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֥ם שְׁמ֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Unto this day they do according to the former manners: they do not fear YHWH, nor do they do according to their statutes or according to their ordinances, or according to the law or according to the commandment which YHWH commanded the children of Ya'aqov, whom he named Yisra'el;

notes.official: *ʿaḏ hayyôm hazzeh hēm ʿōśîm kammišpāṭîm hāriʾšōnîm* 'Unto this day they do according to the former manners' (`ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh-aetiological-formula`; `mishpat-manner-custom-2-kings-17`). Verses 34-40 describe the descendants of the northern Israelites by the standard of the covenant: they 'do not fear YHWH', which contradicts vv 32-33 on the settlers and has long been explained as a separate, later layer (Cogan, *Imperialism and Religion*, 1974; Cogan and Tadmor). *kəḥuqqōṯām ûḵəmišpāṭām wəḵattôrâ wəḵammiṣwâ* 'according to their statutes or according to their ordinances, or according to the law or according to the commandment': in this legal series *mišpāṭ* is 'ordinance' (as 1 Kgs 6:12; 8:58) and *tôrâ* 'law' (`torah-law-deuteronomistic-kings`). *ʾăšer-śām šəmô yiśrāʾēl* 'whom he named Yisra'el' (Gen 32:29; 35:10).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּכְרֹ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה אִתָּם֙ בְּרִ֔ית וַיְצַוֵּ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תִֽירְא֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וְלֹא־תִשְׁתַּחֲו֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם וְלֹ֣א תַעַבְד֔וּם וְלֹ֥א תִזְבְּח֖וּ לָהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: with whom YHWH cut a covenant, and commanded them, saying, "You shall not fear other elohim, nor bow down to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them;

notes.official: *wayyiḵrōṯ YHWH ʾittām bərîṯ* 'with whom YHWH cut a covenant' (central `karat-brit-cut-covenant`). *lōʾ ṯîrəʾû ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm wəlōʾ-ṯištaḥăwû lāhem* 'You shall not fear other elohim, nor bow down to them' (Ex 20:3, 5; `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 4; central `elohim-aherim-other-gods-monolatry-vs-monotheism-scholarly-dispute-cross-corpus`). The fourfold 'fear ... bow down ... serve ... sacrifice' is answered point by point in v 36.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י אִֽם־אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֩ הֶעֱלָ֨ה אֶתְכֶ֜ם מֵאֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם בְּכֹ֧חַ גָּד֛וֹל וּבִזְר֥וֹעַ נְטוּיָ֖ה אֹת֣וֹ תִירָ֑אוּ וְל֥וֹ תִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ וְל֥וֹ תִזְבָּֽחוּ׃

i18n.en: but YHWH, who brought you up out of the land of Mitzrayim with great power and with an outstretched arm, him you shall fear, and to him you shall bow down, and to him you shall sacrifice;

notes.official: *bəḵōaḥ gāḏôl ûḇizrôaʿ nəṭûyâ* 'with great power and with an outstretched arm' (Deut 9:29; cf. 1 Kgs 8:42). *ʾōṯô ṯîrāʾû wəlô ṯištaḥăwû wəlô ṯizbāḥû* 'him you shall fear, and to him you shall bow down, and to him you shall sacrifice': the fronted objects stress exclusivity.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־הַחֻקִּ֨ים וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֜ים וְהַתּוֹרָ֤ה וְהַמִּצְוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּתַ֣ב לָכֶ֔ם תִּשְׁמְר֥וּן לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת כָּל־הַיָּמִ֑ים וְלֹ֥א תִֽירְא֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִֽים׃

i18n.en: and the statutes and the ordinances and the law and the commandment which he wrote for you, you shall be careful to do all the days; and you shall not fear other elohim;

notes.official: *wəʾeṯ-haḥuqqîm wəʾeṯ-hammišpāṭîm wəhattôrâ wəhammiṣwâ ʾăšer kāṯaḇ lāḵem* 'and the statutes and the ordinances and the law and the commandment which he wrote for you': a written law, the Deuteronomic book (`torah-law-deuteronomistic-kings`; `mishpat-manner-custom-2-kings-17`). *wəlōʾ ṯîrəʾû ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm* 'and you shall not fear other elohim' (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 4).

paragraphs.text: וְהַבְּרִ֛ית אֲשֶׁר־כָּרַ֥תִּי אִתְּכֶ֖ם לֹ֣א תִשְׁכָּ֑חוּ וְלֹ֥א תִֽירְא֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִֽים׃

i18n.en: and the covenant that I have cut with you, you shall not forget; and you shall not fear other elohim;

notes.official: *wəhabbərîṯ ʾăšer-kāraṯtî ʾittəḵem lōʾ ṯiškāḥû* 'and the covenant that I have cut with you, you shall not forget' (central `karat-brit-cut-covenant`; Deut 4:23). The speaker shifts to YHWH in the first person. 'other elohim' (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 4).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֛י אִֽם־אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם תִּירָ֑אוּ וְהוּא֙ יַצִּ֣יל אֶתְכֶ֔ם מִיַּ֖ד כָּל־אֹיְבֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: but YHWH your Elohim you shall fear; and he will deliver you out of the hand of all your enemies."

notes.official: *kî ʾim-ʾeṯ-YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵem tîrāʾû* 'but YHWH your Elohim you shall fear' (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 3).

paragraphs.text: וְלֹ֖א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ כִּ֛י אִֽם־כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֥ם הָֽרִאשׁ֖וֹן הֵ֥ם עֹשִֽׂים׃

i18n.en: But they did not listen, but did according to their former manner.

notes.official: *kî ʾim-kəmišpāṭām hāriʾšôn hēm ʿōśîm* 'but did according to their former manner' (`mishpat-manner-custom-2-kings-17`; see v 34).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּהְי֣וּ ׀ הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֗לֶּה יְרֵאִים֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה וְאֶת־פְּסִֽילֵיהֶ֖ם הָי֣וּ עֹֽבְדִ֑ים גַּם־בְּנֵיהֶ֣ם ׀ וּבְנֵ֣י בְנֵיהֶ֗ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֤וּ אֲבֹתָם֙ הֵ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: So these nations feared YHWH, and served their carved images; their children also, and their children's children — as their fathers did, so they do, unto this day.

notes.official: *wəʾeṯ-pəsîlêhem hāyû ʿōḇəḏîm* 'and served their carved images': *pəsîlîm*, plural of *pesel*, rendered as at Ex 20:4 (central `pesel-utemunah-graven-image-iconographic-prohibition-cross-corpus`; ASV 'graven images'). The verse returns to the settlers of vv 24-33 and closes with *ʿaḏ hayyôm hazzeh* 'unto this day' (`ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh-aetiological-formula`). The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) closes the chapter.
